incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Serving runtime errors increasing in prod region us-west-2 for model-serving. 50% error rate on inference -> paging on-call. thread_ts=2491234567

Mike (SRE): grabbing this. seeing rapid scale events in the autoscaler logs, lots of nodes added then immediately removed. possible feedback loop.

Jen (DevOps): yep, autoscaler metric stream shows spike in pending pods -> scale up -> new nodes report CUDA OOMs and crashloop -> nodes evicted -> back to pending -> repeat. dashboards: https://redwood.internal/d/serve/auto-scale?from=now-1h

Ben (Runtime): logs from gpu-runtime show repeated ``CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY`` during model init. stack: ``nvml_device_reset``, process restart. Suspect batch sizing + quantized kernel mismatch on new nodes' driver version.

Cara (on-call): quick mitigation plan: 1) pause autoscaler (set controller.k8s.io/paused=true) 2) scale down replicas to stable capacity 3) cordon suspicious nodes 4) route traffic to fallback region (us-east-1) for critical customers. doing now.

Jen (DevOps): running:
```bash
kubectl patch hpa/model-serving -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":3,"maxReplicas":6}}'
kubectl annotate hpa/model-serving controller.k8s.io/paused=true --overwrite
```
Applying now.

Mike (SRE): cordoned nodes: n-gpu-37, n-gpu-38, n-gpu-41. draining one to check container state: ``kubectl drain n-gpu-37 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data``

Ben (Runtime): pulled container logs from drained node, snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T02:18:41Z] initializing model shards
[2026-03-15T02:18:45Z] Allocating 14.7GB on GPU0
[2026-03-15T02:18:46Z] CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY at allocate_kernel
[2026-03-15T02:18:46Z] process killed, restart backoff
```
Also found driver mismatch on the node: nvidia-driver 525.x vs expected 535.x. New nodes came from a different image.

Cara (on-call): copying runbook snippet for degraded serving: "if OOMs coincide with scale-up, reduce batch_size and pin model to smaller kv-cache until node image compiles."

Liz (Customer Ops): heads up, 3 enterprise customers (acme-inc, delta-analytics, brightpay) reported increased 5xxs around 02:15. I just opened a high-priority CS ticket and emailed account reps. Customers need ETA and fallback confirmation.

Mike (SRE): temporarily routing traffic: updating routing policy to prefer us-east-1 for enterprise-tagged requests. command: ``routectl set-region-preference --service model-serving --region us-east-1 --tag enterprise --ttl 10m``

Jen (DevOps): started a targeted node image rollback to the previous AMI with driver 535.x in the autoscaler launch template. rolling 2 nodes at a time.

Ben (Runtime): also pushing a hotfix to the container: graceful OOM handling patch and lowered default batch_size from 8 -> 4. small image pushed to canary tag: ``redwood/runtime:canary-20260315-oomfix``

deploy-bot: deploy started: redwood/runtime:canary-20260315-oomfix -> cluster-us-west-2 (canary)

Cara (on-call): monitoring canary. if stable for 10m we'll bump nodes and unpause autoscaler with damping.

Mike (SRE): observed customer error-rate drop for the routed enterprise traffic to <2% after region switch. overall error-rate marginally down. still seeing restart loops on the remaining new nodes.

Ben (Runtime): quick config to push to prod to avoid re-triggering scale: set autoscaler cooldown to 5m and enable scale-damping:```
kubectl patch cm autoscaler-config -p '{"data":{"scaleCooldown":"300s","dampingFactor":"0.6"}}'
```

Jen (DevOps): applied cooldown/damping. will watch for any additional scale events.

Cara (on-call): customer impact note: impact window ~02:12-02:30 UTC. affected ~12k requests/min at peak, ~3 enterprise customers with partial downtime. we escalated and routed to fallback region.

Liz (Customer Ops): messaging ready for CS: short incident summary, mitigation done, next steps include postmortem and timeline, ETA for full remediation 4-6 hours while we finish image rollback and a full sweep.

Mike (SRE): handing off to Alice (night) for longer-term remediation and postmortem. Alice please confirm you have runbook and access to throttles, routing, and the AMI rollback notes.

Alice (Night): taking over. confirmed I can access runbooks and ``routectl``. I'll coordinate with Ben to validate the hotfix across remaining nodes and follow up on a postmortem doc. will update in 30m.

Ben (Runtime): follow-ups/TODOs (added as quick checklist):
- Open ticket INF-4321 for image drift and autoscaler launch template mismatch
- Backfill e2e tests for driver compatibility on new AMI
- Add proactive alert: consecutive OOM restarts > 3 in 10m -> scale-pause auto-toggle
- Add canary gating for new node images to prevent autoscaler from using unvalidated AMIs

Cara (on-call): slack reaction: :thumbsup: good handoff. Adding incident severity and customers to pager duty ticket.

incident-bot: Incident update posted to status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INV-20260315-01

Alice (Night): noted. starting remediation loop and will post timeline + initial postmortem notes in #incidents thread. closing active pager for now but keeping thread open for updates.

Liz (Customer Ops): I'll send a short apology + mitigation summary to affected customers and offer a follow-up call for enterprise accounts.

Mike (SRE): final quick note: probable root cause = autoscaler picked new AMI/images without validated GPU driver and mismatch exposed OOMs at scale; coupled with aggressive scale-up/scale-down settings created a feedback loop. fixes: AMI gate + cooldown + runtime OOM handling + canary.

Alice (Night): acknowledged. last_message_ts=2491234620"
